Europe in 1350 looks calm on the map. Underneath the borders, between 30% and 60% of the population had died in three years. Here is what the colors hide.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The plague reached Sicily in October 1347 on twelve Genoese galleys, Marseilles by January 1348 and England by June 1348. Florence fell from roughly 110,000-120,000 people in 1338 to about 50,000 in 1351.

2/ The estimates still differ. One historian puts the European death rate near 60%, around 50 million people. Another says 45-50%. Pope Clement VI's agents counted 23.8 million dead in 1351, about 31%.

3/ Persecution followed. About 2,000 Jews were killed in Strasbourg in February 1349, and communities in Mainz and Cologne were destroyed that August. Many survivors went to Poland, where Casimir III welcomed them.

4/ With fewer workers, wages rose and some rents collapsed. Landowners often moved from labour services to money rents to keep tenants. The full story, with Serbia, Prague and the Golden Horde: https://buttondown.com/forummapping
